questions.question: A bucket is drawn from a well by means of a rope which is wound around a wheel of radius 48 cm. If the bucket ascends in 1 minute 12 seconds at a speed of 1.2 m/sec, find the length of the rope.
questions.questionHtml: A bucket is drawn from a well by means of a rope which is wound around a wheel of radius 48 cm. If the bucket ascends in 1 minute 12 seconds at a speed of 1.2 m/sec, find the length of the rope.
questions.solution:
As we know,

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed = 1.2 meter/sec and Time = 1 min 12 sec = 60 + 12 = 72 second

Required Distance = 72 × 1.2 = 86.4 meter

1 meter = 100 cm

86.4 m = 8640 cm

questions.question: A takes 2 hours 30 minutes more than B to walk 40 km. If A doubles his speed, then he can make it in 1 hour less than B. What is the average time taken by A and B to walk a 40 km distance?
questions.questionHtml: A takes 2 hours 30 minutes more than B to walk 40 km. If A doubles his speed, then he can make it in 1 hour less than B. What is the average time taken by A and B to walk a 40 km distance?
questions.solution:
Given:

A takes 2 hours 30 minutes more than B to walk 40 km.

If A doubles his speed, then he can make it in 1 hour less than B.

Formula used:

Speed = Distance/Time

Calculations:

Let the initial speeds of A and B be x and y respectively and the time taken by A and B be tA and tB respectively.

tA = 40/x

tB = 40/y

tA - tB = 40/x - 40/y

⇒ 40/x - 40/y = 2.5      ----(i)

After A doubles his speed,

⇒ 40/y - 40/2x = 1      ----(ii)

On adding equation (i) and (ii),

40/x - 40/2x = 2.5 + 1

⇒ 40/x - 20/x = 3.5

⇒ 20/x = 3.5

⇒ x = 40/7 km/h

From equation (ii),

40/y - 40/2x = 1

⇒ 40/y - 40/2(40/7) = 1

⇒ 40/y - 7/2 = 1

⇒ 40/y = 1 + 7/2

⇒ 40/y = 9/2

⇒ y = 80/9 km/h

tA = 40/x

⇒ tA = 40/(40/7)

⇒ tA = 7 hours

tB = 40/y

⇒ 40/(80/9)

⇒ 9/2 hours

Average time of A and B = {7 + (9/2)}/2

⇒ 23/4 hours

⇒ 5 hours 45 minutes

∴ The average time taken by A and B to walk a 40 km distance is 5 hours 45 minutes. 

Shortcut Trick 

Speed ratio of A      Old   :  New 

Speed ratio of A       1            2

Time Ratio of A         2            1 

Here, time difference is 1 unit.

And according to question time difference is 2.5 + 1 = 3.5 hr

​⇒ 1 unit = 3.5 hr

​⇒ 2 unit = 7 hr 

So, the time taken by A is = 7 h

​⇒ Time taken by B is = 7 - 2.5 = 4.5 h

​⇒ Average time taken = (7 + 4.5)/2 = 5.75 hr 

​⇒ 5.75 hr = 5 hour and 45 minutes 

∴ The average time taken by A and B to walk a 40 km distance is 5 hours 45 minutes.

questions.question: Rashi travelled a distance of 400 km at an average speed of 50 km/h. She covers the first half distance in the first lag in 2 hours, while she covers another lag at half the speed of that of the first lag in 1 hour. What is the speed (in km/h) of the remaining distance?
questions.questionHtml: Rashi travelled a distance of 400 km at an average speed of 50 km/h. She covers the first half distance in the first lag in 2 hours, while she covers another lag at half the speed of that of the first lag in 1 hour. What is the speed (in km/h) of the remaining distance?
questions.solution:
Total distance = 400 km, Average speed = 50 km/h, First half (200 km) in 2 hrs, second lag at half speed (50 km/h) in 1 hr


First lag speed = 200 km / 2 hrs = 100 km/h, second lag speed = 100 km/h / 2 = 50 km/h, Distance covered in second lag = 50 km/h × 1 hr = 50 km

Total distance covered in first two lags = 200 km + 50 km = 250 km, Remaining distance = 400 km - 250 km = 150 km

Total time = 400 km / 50 km/h = 8 hrs, Time for first two lags = 2 hrs + 1 hr = 3 hrs, Remaining time = 8 hrs - 3 hrs = 5 hrs, Remaining speed = 150 km / 5 hrs = 30 km/h

questions.question: A bus starts from a bus stand after every 50 minutes in the same direction. Mohit is walking in opposite direction with a speed of 50 km / hr . If Mohit meets each bus in 10 minutes, then what is the speed of bus?
questions.questionHtml: A bus starts from a bus stand after every 50 minutes in the same direction. Mohit is walking in opposite direction with a speed of 50 km/hr. If Mohit meets each bus in 10 minutes, then what is the speed of bus?
questions.solution:
Distance covered by bus in (50 - 10) = 40 minutes = The distance travelled by Mohit in 10 minutes.

Distance covered by bus in 40/60 = The distance travelled by Mohit in 10/60.

⇒ 40x/60 = 50 × 10/60 ⇒ x = 12.5

questions.question: With a speed of 48 km/h, Raghu is able to complete his journey in 2 hours 28 minutes. If he wants to cover the same distance in 1 hour 36 minutes, then what should be his new speed?
questions.questionHtml: With a speed of 48 km/h, Raghu is able to complete his journey in 2 hours 28 minutes. If he wants to cover the same distance in 1 hour 36 minutes, then what should be his new speed?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since Distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time (S1 × T1 = S2 × T2).

Convert times to minutes: T1 = 148 min and T2 = 96 min.

Ratio of Time = 148 : 96 = 37 : 24.

Ratio of Speed = 24 : 37.

If 24 units = 48 km/h, then 1 unit = 2 km/h ∴ 37 units = 37 × 2 = 74 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 74 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Speed (S1) = 48 km/h

Initial Time (T1) = 2 hr 28 min = (2 × 60) + 28 = 148 min

New Time (T2) = 1 hr 36 min = (1 × 60) + 36 = 96 min

Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Distance (D) = S1 × T1

⇒ D = 48 × (148/60) km

⇒ New Speed (S2) = D ÷ T2

⇒ S2 = [48 × (148/60)] ÷ (96/60)

⇒ S2 = (48 × 148) ÷ 96

⇒ S2 = 148 ÷ 2

⇒ S2 = 74 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 74 km/h.

Additional Information

Speed-Time Inverse Relation

When Distance is fixed, the ratio of speeds is the inverse of the ratio of times taken (S1:S2 = T2:T1).

Unit Conversion

To convert Speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

For a journey with different speeds but equal distances, Average Speed = 2S1S2 ÷ (S1 + S2).

questions.question: A takes 2 hours more than B to cover a distance of 40 km. If A doubles his speed, he takes \(1\frac{1}{2}\) hour more than B to cover 80 km. To cover a distance of 120 km, how much time (in hours) will B take travelling at his same speed?
questions.questionHtml: A takes 2 hours more than B to cover a distance of 40 km. If A doubles his speed, he takes \(1\frac{1}{2}\) hour more than B to cover 80 km. To cover a distance of 120 km, how much time (in hours) will B take travelling at his same speed?
questions.solution:
Alternate Method Time taken by A to cover  40 km distance = t + 2 hours, where t is the time taken by B to cover the distance.

Time taken by A to cover the 40 km distance when its speed is double = Time taken to cover 80 km distance/2 = (2t + 3/2)/2 = t + 3/4

Distance = (S1 × S2)/(S1 - S2) [Time difference]

Here, S1 = x, S2 = 2x (For A)

40 = 2x × x/(2x - x)[t + 2 - t - 3/4]

⇒ 40 = 2x(5/4)

⇒ x = 16

Actual time taken by A = 40/16 = 2.5 hours

Actual time taken by B = 2.5 -  2 = 0.5 hour

Speed of B = 40/0.5 = 80 km/h

Required time taken by B = 120/80 = 3/2 hours

Traditional method:

Given:

A takes 2 hours more than B to cover a distance of 40 km

When A doubles his speed, he takes 1.5 hours more than B to travel 80 km

Concept used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

Let The speed B be x km/h.

Time taken by B to cover 40km = 40/x hour

Time taken by A to cover 40km = [(40/x) + 2] hour

Speed of A = (40)/[(40 + 2)/x] kmph

⇒ (20x)/(20 + x) kmph ……… (1)

Now,

Time taken by B to cover 80 km = 80/x hour

When A doubles his speed = (40x)/(20 + x) kmph

Time taken by A to cover 80 km = 80/(40x)/(20 + x)

⇒ (40 + 2x)/x hour

Now in this case,

A takes 1.5 hour more than B to travel 80 km

So,

⇒ (40 + 2x)/x - 80/x = 3/2

⇒ (40 + 2x - 80)/x = 3/2

⇒ 4x - 80 = 3x

⇒ x = 80

So,

Speed of B is 80 kmph.

Now,

To cover a distance of 120 km, B will take

⇒ 120/80 = 1.5 hours

∴ To cover a distance of 120 km, B will take 1.5 hours.

Shortcut TrickLet, time taken by B = t hours and, A = t + 2

Now, the speed of B = 40/t kmph and the speed of A = 40/(t + 2) kmph

We know, Distance = Speed × time

To travel a distance of 80 km A doubles his speed

A takes = \(\frac{80}{\frac{80}{t+2}}\) = (t + 2) hours

B takes = 80/(40/t) = 2t hours

According to the question,

t + 2 - 2t = \(1\frac{1}{2}\)

⇒ t = 1/2

Now B takes 1/2 hours to cover 40 km

∴ B will travel 120 km in (3 × 1/2) = 3/2 hours = \(1\frac{1}{2}\) hours

questions.question: A person travels a distance of 240 km, partly by train and the rest by bus. He takes \(3\frac{1}{2}\) hours if he travels 150 km by train and the rest by bus. If he travels 140 km by bus and the rest by train, he takes \(3\frac{2}{3}\) hours. What is the speed of the train?
questions.questionHtml: A person travels a distance of 240 km, partly by train and the rest by bus. He takes \(3\frac{1}{2}\) hours if he travels 150 km by train and the rest by bus. If he travels 140 km by bus and the rest by train, he takes \(3\frac{2}{3}\) hours. What is the speed of the train?
questions.solution:
Let speed of train and bus x km/hr and y km/hr respectively

According to the question,

⇒ 150/x + 90/y = 7/2

Divided by 3

⇒ 50/x + 30/y = 7/6     ----(1)

100/x + 140/y = 11/3

Divided by 2

⇒ 50/x + 70/y = 11/6      ----((2)

Subtract equation (1) from equation (2)

⇒ 40/y = 4/6

⇒ y = 60 km/hr

From equation (1)

⇒ 50/x + 30/60 = 7/6

⇒ 50/x + 1/2 = 7/6

⇒ 50/x = 7/6 – 1/2

⇒ 50/x = (7 – 3)/6 = 4/6

⇒ x = 50 × (6/4)

⇒ x = 75 km/hr

Speed of train 75 km/hr

questions.question: Akhil takes 30 minutes extra to cover a distance of 150 km if he drives 10 km/h slower than his usual speed. How much time will be take to drive 90 km if he drives 15 km per hour slower than his usual speed?
questions.questionHtml: Akhil takes 30 minutes extra to cover a distance of 150 km if he drives 10 km/h slower than his usual speed. How much time will be take to drive 90 km if he drives 15 km per hour slower than his usual speed?
questions.solution:
Given:

Akhil takes 30 minutes i.e., 1/2 hour extra to cover a distance of 150 km if he drives 10 km/h slower than his usual speed.

Concept used:

Time = D/S

D = Distance

T = Time 

Calculation:

Let the usual speed of Akhil be S km/h.

After a 10kmph reduction, the speed of Akhil = (S - 10) km/h

According to the question,

150/(S - 10) - 150/S = 1/2

⇒ 150 {1/(S - 10) - 1/S} = 1/2

⇒ 150 {(S - S + 10)/ {S × (S -10)} = 1/2

⇒ 150 {10/ {S × (S - 10)} = 1/2

⇒ S × (S - 10) = 2 × 150 × 10

⇒ S = 60

Now,

Time taken by Akhil to drive 90 km at (60 - 15) km/h i.e. 45km/h

⇒ (90/45) hours

⇒ 2 hours

∴ Time taken by Akhil to drive 90 km if he drives 15 km per hour slower than his usual speed is 2 hours.

questions.question: A person moved from place A for place B at 2 p.m. at a speed of 4.5 km/h, stayed at place B for 1.5 hours and returned to place A at a speed of 6 km/h. He came back to place A at 7 p.m. What is the distance between places A and B (in km)?
questions.questionHtml: A person moved from place A for place B at 2 p.m. at a speed of 4.5 km/h, stayed at place B for 1.5 hours and returned to place A at a speed of 6 km/h. He came back to place A at 7 p.m. What is the distance between places A and B (in km)?
questions.solution:
Alternate MethodDistance = (X × Y)(X + Y) × [Total time]

⇒ (6 × 4.5)/(6 + 4.5) × (5 - 1.5)

⇒ (6 × 4.5 × 3.5)/10.5

⇒ 9 km

Traditional method:

Given:

A person moved from place A for place B at 2 p.m. at a speed of 4.5 km/h, stayed at place B for 1.5 hours and returned to place A at a speed of 6 km/h.

Concept used:

Distance = speed × time

Calculations:

Let the distance from A to B is ' x ' km

His total time of travelling = 5 - 1.5 = 3.5 hours      (he took a rest of 1.5 hours)

Now, 

Time of travelling from A to B/Ttime of travelling from B to A = Speed from B to A/Speed from A to B          (speed and time are inversely proportional)

Time of travelling of A/Ttime of travelling of B = 6/4.5

⇒ 4/3 

Time of travel from A to B = (4/7) × 3.5 = 2 hours 

Time of travel from B to A = (3/7) × 3.5 = 1.5 hours

Total distance = 4.5 × 2 = 9km  

∴ The correct choice is option 4.

questions.question: Diameter of wheel of a cycle is 7 cm. A cyclist takes 75 minutes to reach a destination at the speed of 36.3 km/hr. How many revolutions will the wheel make during the journey?
questions.questionHtml: Diameter of wheel of a cycle is 7 cm. A cyclist takes 75 minutes to reach a destination at the speed of 36.3 km/hr. How many revolutions will the wheel make during the journey?
questions.solution:
Total distance covered in 1 revolution = 2πr = πd = (22/7) × 7 = 0.22 m

Total distance covered in journey = (Speed) × (Time) = 36.3 × (75/60) = 45.375 km = 45375 m

Total number of revolution = 45375/0.22 = 206250

questions.question: A train takes \(2\frac{1}{2}\) hours less for a journey of 300 km, if its speed is increased by 20 km/h from its usual speed. How much time will it take to cover a distance of 192 km at its usual speed?
questions.questionHtml: A train takes \(2\frac{1}{2}\)hours less for a journey of 300 km, if its speed is increased by 20 km/h from its usual speed. How much time will it take to cover a distance of 192 km at its usual speed?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

\(2\frac{1}{2} = \frac{5}{2}\)

Let speed of train be x km/hr

According to the question

[300/x] – [300/(x + 20)] = 5/2

⇒ 300 [x + 20 – x]/[x (x + 20) = 5/2

⇒ 6000/(x2 + 20x) = 5/2

⇒ 12000 = 5x2 + 100x

⇒ x2 + 20x – 2400 = 0

⇒ x2 + 60x – 40x – 2400 = 0

⇒ x (x + 60) – 40 (x + 60) = 0

⇒ (x + 60) (x – 40) = 0

Taking,

⇒ (x – 40) = 0

⇒ x = 40 km/hr

Speed of the train = 40 km/hr

questions.question: Anand covers a certain distance in the first lag of 5 hours at the speed of 50 km/h. In the second lag, he increased the speed by 20% due to which he covered 20% extra distance than that of the first lag. He covered the third lag at the average speed of the first two lags and covered 10% extra distance than that of the second lag distance. How much total time (in hours) did he take to complete all three lags?
questions.questionHtml: Anand covers a certain distance in the first lag of 5 hours at the speed of 50 km/h. In the second lag, he increased the speed by 20% due to which he covered 20% extra distance than that of the first lag. He covered the third lag at the average speed of the first two lags and covered 10% extra distance than that of the second lag distance. How much total time (in hours) did he take to complete all three lags?
questions.solution:
Distance = 50 × 5 = 250 km

Distance = 250 + 250 × 120/100 = 300 km

Speed = 50 + 50 × 120/100 = 60 km/hr

Time = 300/60 = 5 hours

Distance = 300 + 300 × 110/100 = 330 km

Speed = (60 + 50)/2 = 55 km/hr

Time = 330/55 = 6 hours

Total time = 5 + 5 + 6 = 16 hours

questions.question: The speed of a train including stoppages is 75 kmph and excluding stoppages, the speed of the train is 90 kmph. For how many minutes does the train stop per hour?
questions.questionHtml: The speed of a train including stoppages is 75 kmph and excluding stoppages, the speed of the train is 90 kmph. For how many minutes does the train stop per hour?
questions.solution:
Due to stoppage in 1 hour it covers = (90 – 75) km = 15 km less

Time taken by train in stoppage = 15/90 = 1/6 hour = 10 minutes

questions.question: If Abhi travels a certain distance at 6 km/h, he reaches his destination 12 minutes early, but if he travels at 4 km/h, he reaches his destination 10 minutes late. The speed (in km/h) at which he should travel to reach his destination on time is ______.
questions.questionHtml: If Abhi travels a certain distance at 6 km/h, he reaches his destination 12 minutes early, but if he travels at 4 km/h, he reaches his destination 10 minutes late. The speed (in km/h) at which he should travel to reach his destination on time is ______.
questions.solution:
Let right time for the man to cover its journey (in minutes) be x min, then

As we know,

Distance = Speed × Time

According to the question

6 × (x - 12) /60 = 4 × (x + 10) /60

3 (x - 12) = 2 (x + 10)

3x - 36 = 2x + 20

3x – 2x = 36 + 20

x = 56 min

Speed of the man =\(\frac{{6(56 - 12)}}{{60 \times \frac{{56}}{{60}}}} = \frac{{6 \times 44}}{{56}} = \frac{{33}}{7} = 4\frac{5}{{7}}\)

questions.question: A fast local of Mumbai takes 45 minutes less than a slow local for a journey of 150 km. If the speed of the fast local is 10 km/h more than that of the slow local, find the speed (in km/h) of the slow local train.
questions.questionHtml: A fast local of Mumbai takes 45 minutes less than a slow local for a journey of 150 km. If the speed of the fast local is 10 km/h more than that of the slow local, find the speed (in km/h) of the slow local train.
questions.solution:
Let the speed of the slow train = x km/h

AQT,

Speed of the fast train = Speed of the slow train + 10 = x + 10

Time of fast train = Time of slow train - \(\frac{3}{4}\)

\(\frac{150}{x\ + \ 10} =\frac{150}{x} - \frac{3}{4} \) ⇒ \( \frac{150}{x}\ - \frac{150}{x\ + \ 10}= \frac{3}{4}\) ⇒ \(\frac{150x \ +\ 1500 \ - 150x }{x^2\ + \ 10x} = \frac{3}{4}\) ⇒ \(\frac{1500}{x^2 \ + 10} = \frac{3}{4}\)

⇒ x2 + 10x - 2000 = 0 ⇒ x2 + 50x - 40x + 2000 = 0 ⇒ (x + 50)(x - 40) = 0 ⇒ x = 40, - 50

The speed of the slow train (x) = 40 km/h and The speed of the fast train (x + 10) = 50 km/h

questions.question: A and B started traveling towards each other at the same time, from places X to Y and Y to X, respectively. After crossing each other, A and B took 2.45 hours and 4.05 hours to reach Y and X, respectively. If the speed of B was 8.4 km/h, then what was the speed (in km/h) of A?
questions.questionHtml: A and B started traveling towards each other at the same time, from places X to Y and Y to X, respectively. After crossing each other, A and B took 2.45 hours and 4.05 hours to reach Y and X, respectively. If the speed of B was 8.4 km/h, then what was the speed (in km/h) of A?
questions.solution:
Given:

After Crossing A took =  2.45 hours

After Crossing B took = 4.05 hours

Speed of B = 8.4 km/h

Concept used:

In such types of questions where time, after the crossing is given there following formula is used.

Speed of A/Speed of B = √[Time taken by B to reach X after crossing/Time taken by A to reach X after crossing]

Calculation:

Speed of A/8.4 = √(4.05/2.45) = √(81/49) = 9/7

Speed of A = (9/7) × 8.4 = 10.8 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 10.8 km/hr.

questions.question: A car starts from point A towards point B, travelling at the speed of 20 km/h. 1 \(\frac{1}{2}\) hours later, another car starts from point A and travelling at the speed of 30 km/h and reaches 2 \(\frac{1}{2}\) hours before the first car. Find the distance between A and B.
questions.questionHtml: A car starts from point A towards point B, travelling at the speed of 20 km/h. 1\(\frac{1}{2}\)hours later, another car starts from point A and travelling at the speed of 30 km/h and reaches 2\(\frac{1}{2}\)hours before the first car. Find the distance between A and B.
questions.solution:
Let the total distance be x km, in 1.5 hr 1st car travel 30 km, remaining (x - 30) km

So, according to the question.

⇒ \(\frac{(x - 30)}{20} - \frac{x}{30}\) = 2.5 ⇒ x - 90 = 150 ⇒ x = 240 km

questions.question: If a train runs with the speed of 72 km/h, it reaches its destination late by 15 minutes. However, if its speed is 90 km/h, it is late by only 5 minutes. The correct time to cover its journey in minutes is:
questions.questionHtml: If a train runs with the speed of 72 km/h, it reaches its destination late by 15 minutes. However, if its speed is 90 km/h, it is late by only 5 minutes. The correct time to cover its journey in minutes is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A train runs with the speed of 72 km/h, it reaches its destination late = 15 minutes

A train runs with the speed of 90 km/h, it reaches its destination late = 5 minutes

Formula used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Concept used:

Distance is same

Calculation:

Let the correct time to covers its journey be x min

According to the question

⇒ 72 × (x + 15)/60 = 90 × (x + 5)/60

⇒ 4 × (x + 15) = 5 × (x + 5)

⇒ 4x + 60 = 5x + 25

⇒ (5x – 4x) = (60 – 25)

⇒ x = 35 min

∴ The correct time to covers its journey is 35 min

questions.question: A car takes 50 minutes to cover a certain distance at a speed of 54 km/h. If the speed is increased by 25%, then how long will it take to cover three-fourth of the same distance?
questions.questionHtml: A car takes 50 minutes to cover a certain distance at a speed of 54 km/h. If the speed is increased by 25%, then how long will it take to cover three-fourth of the same distance?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed ratio = 100 : 125 = 4 : 5

Time ratio (for same distance) = inverse of speed ratio = 5 : 4

Initial time 5 units = 50 minutes ⇒ 1 unit = 10 minutes

Time for full distance at new speed = 4 units = 40 minutes

Time for 3/4 distance = 3/4 × 40 minutes = 30 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 30 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial speed (S1) = 54 km/h

Initial time (T1) = 50 minutes = 50/60 hours

Formula used: Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Total Distance = 54 × (50/60) = 45 km

⇒ New Speed = 54 + (25/100) × 54 = 54 + 13.5 = 67.5 km/h

⇒ New Distance = 3/4 × 45 = 33.75 km

⇒ New Time = New Distance ÷ New Speed

⇒ New Time = 33.75 ÷ 67.5 = 0.5 hours

⇒ New Time in minutes = 0.5 × 60 = 30 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 30 minutes.

Additional Information

Speed-Time Relationship

For a constant distance, speed is inversely proportional to time (S1/S2 = T2/T1).

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. For two equal distances with speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy/(x+y).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: A man is walking at a speed of 14 km/h. After every km, he takes rest for 7 minutes. How much time will he take to cover a distance of 7 km?
questions.questionHtml: A man is walking at a speed of 14 km/h. After every km, he takes rest for 7 minutes. How much time will he take to cover a distance of 7 km?
questions.solution:
If the man doesn't stop to rest, then

Time taken to complete the distance of 7 km = 7/14 = 1/2 h = 30 min 

Total rest time = 7 × 6 = 42 min

Total time to cover the distance = 30 + 42 = 72 min = 1\(\frac{1}{5}\) hours

questions.question: A car moves a distance of 600 km with uniform speed. The number of hours taken for the journey is \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the number representing speed in km/h. The time taken to cover the distance is:
questions.questionHtml: A car moves a distance of 600 km with uniform speed. The number of hours taken for the journey is \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the number representing speed in km/h. The time taken to cover the distance is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The number of hours taken for the journey is 2/3 of the speed

Distance = 600 km

Formula Used:

Distance = Time × Speed

Calculation:

Suppose the number of hours for the journey is 2x and the speed is 3x.

⇒ Distance = Time × Speed

⇒ 600 = 2x × 3x

⇒ x2 = 600/6

⇒ x2 = 100

⇒ x = √100

⇒ x = 10

∴ Time taken to cover distance = 2x = 20 hours

questions.question: A part of a journey is covered in 37.5 minutes at 90 km/h and the remaining part in 14 minutes at 80 km/h. The total distance (in km} of the journey is:
questions.questionHtml: A part of a journey is covered in 37.5 minutes at 90 km/h and the remaining part in 14 minutes at 80 km/h. The total distance (in km} of the journey is:

questions.question: During his morning walk, Atul walks for 45 minutes at a speed of 8 km/h and takes 15 rounds of a park. Shekhar takes 10 rounds of the same park in 40 minutes. What is the speed of Shekhar in km/h?
questions.questionHtml: During his morning walk, Atul walks for 45 minutes at a speed of 8 km/h and takes 15 rounds of a park. Shekhar takes 10 rounds of the same park in 40 minutes. What is the speed of Shekhar in km/h?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of Atul = 8 km/h

Shekhar completes 10 rounds in 40 minutes

Concept used:

Distance = Speed × time

Using unitary method to solve question

Calculation:

In 45 minutes Atul cover 8 × 45/60 = 6 km

So, 15 rounds = 6 km

So, 10 rounds = 4 km

So, Shekhar covers 4 km in 40 minutes

So, his speed is 6 km/h

∴ The speed of Shekhar is 6 km/h

questions.question: A person takes 40 minutes more than his usual time when he covers a distance of 20 km at 5 km/h. If he covers the same distance at 8 km/h, he takes x minutes less than the usual time. What is the value of x?
questions.questionHtml: A person takes 40 minutes more than his usual time when he covers a distance of 20 km at 5 km/h. If he covers the same distance at 8 km/h, he takes x minutes less than the usual time. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of man = 5 km/h

Distance = 20 km

Formula used:

Speed = Distance / Time

Calculation:

As we know,

Time = Distance/Speed = 20/5 = 4 hr

Usual time = 4 hr – 40 min = 3 hr and 20 min

Second condition

Speed of man = 8 km/hr

Time = Distance /Speed = 20/8 = 2 hr 30 min

Time difference = (3 hr + 20 min) – (2 hr + 30 min) = 50 min 

Shortcut Trick

According to the question,

⇒ [(5 × 8)/(8 – 5)] × [(40 + x)/60] = 20

⇒ [40/3] × [(40 + x)/60] = 20 

⇒ (40 + x) = (20 × 60 × 3)/40 = 90

⇒ x = 90 – 40

∴ x = 50

questions.question: A bus covered 360 km in 6 hours. If it travels at one-fourth of its usual speed, then how much more time will it take to cover the same distance?
questions.questionHtml: A bus covered 360 km in 6 hours. If it travels at one-fourth of its usual speed, then how much more time will it take to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
Given:

A bus covered 360 km in 6 hours

Formula used:

Speed = Distance/time

Calculation:

Usual speed of bus = 360/6 = 60 kmph

If it travels at one-fourth of its usual speed, its speed becomes 1/4 × 60 = 15 kmph

Time taken to cover 360 km with decreased speed = 360/15 = 24 hours

∴ Extra time taken to cover the same distance = 24 - 6 = 18 hours

questions.question: Suman travels from place X to Y and Rekha travels from Y to X, simultaneously. After meeting on the way, Suman and Rekha reach Y and X, in 3 hours 12 minutes and one hour 48 minutes, respectively. If the speed of Rekha is 9 km/h, then the speed (in km/h) of Suman is:
questions.questionHtml: Suman travels from place X to Y and Rekha travels from Y to X, simultaneously. After meeting on the way, Suman and Rekha reach Y and X, in 3 hours 12 minutes and one hour 48 minutes, respectively. If the speed of Rekha is 9 km/h, then the speed (in km/h) of Suman is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Time of Suman = 3 hours 12 min = (3 + 12/60) 

⇒ (3 + 1/5) = 16/5 hrs

Time of Rekha = 1 hours 48 min = (1 + 48/60)

⇒ (1 + 4/5) = 9/5 hrs

Speed of Rekha = 9 km/h

Concept used:

Speed of Suman/Speed of Rekha = √(Time of Rekha/Time of Suman)

Calculation:

Let the speed of Suman be s

According to the question

Speed of Suman/Speed of Rekha = √(Time of Rekha/Time of Suman)

⇒ s/9 = √[(9/5)/(16/5)]

⇒ s/9 = √9/16

⇒ s/9 = 3/4

⇒ 4s = (9 × 3)

⇒ 4s = 27

⇒ s = (27/4)

⇒ s = \(6\frac{3}{4}\) km/h

∴ The speed of Suman is \(6\frac{3}{4}\)

questions.question: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 650 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of 8 km and 10.5 km per hour, respectively. The distance (in metres) between them after 12 minutes is:
questions.questionHtml: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 650 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of 8 km and 10.5 km per hour, respectively. The distance (in metres) between them after 12 minutes is:

Distance traveled by police in 12 mins = 17.5/6 × (12 × 60) = 2100 m

Required Distance  = (650 + 1600) - 2100 = 2250 - 2100 = 150 m

questions.question: A bus covers a 60 kilometre distance in 1 hour 30 minutes, whereas the same distance is covered by a car in 45 minutes. What is the ratio of the speed of the car to the speed of the bus?
questions.questionHtml: A bus covers a 60 kilometre distance in 1 hour 30 minutes, whereas the same distance is covered by a car in 45 minutes. What is the ratio of the speed of the car to the speed of the bus?
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance covered by bus and car = 60 km.

Time taken by bus to cover the distance = 1 hour 30 minutes.

Time taken by car to cover the same distance = 45 minutes.

Formula used:

Speed = Distance/time

Calculation:

Time taken by bus = 1hr 30 min.

⇒ T = (1 + 30/60) = 3/2 hr.

Time taken by car to cover the same distance = 45 minutes.

⇒ T = 45/60 hr = 3/4 hr.

According to question:

Speed of car ∶ Speed of bus 

⇒ [60/(3/4)] ∶ [60/(3/2)] 

⇒ 80 ∶ 40

⇒ 2 ∶ 1

∴ The ratio of the speed of car and bus is 2 : 1

Alternate Method

Concept used:

When the distance is constant, then the speed is inversely proportional to time.

Calculation:

Time covered by bus = 1hr 30 min.

⇒ T2 = (1 + 30/60) hr.

⇒ T2 = 3/2 hr.

again,

Time covered by car = 45 min

⇒ T1 = 45/60 hr.

⇒  T1 = 3/4 hr.

S1 ∶ S2 = (1/T1) ∶ (1/T2)

⇒ 1/(3/4) ∶ 1/(3/2)

⇒ 4/3 ∶ 2/3 = 2 ∶ 1

∴ The ratio of the speed of car and bus is 2 : 1

questions.question: A person covers a distance of 300 km and then returns to the starting point. The time taken by him for the outward journey is 5 hours more than time taken for the return journey. If he returned at a speed of 10 km/h more than the speed of going. What was the speed (in km/h) for the outward journey?
questions.questionHtml: A person covers a distance of 300 km and then returns to the starting point. The time taken by him for the outward journey is 5 hours more than time taken for the return journey. If he returned at a speed of 10 km/h more than the speed of going. What was the speed (in km/h) for the outward journey?
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance covered by the person in a single journey = 300km

Time taken by him for the outward journey = 5 hours more than the time taken for the return journey.

The return speed is 10km/h more than the speed of going.

Formula used:

Distance covered = Speed × Time taken

Calculation:

Let the speed of outward journey be ‘x’ km/h

Hence, the speed of return journey will be (x + 10) km/h

So, time taken in return journey = 300/(x + 10) hours

Time taken in outward journey = (300/x) hours

According to the question,

⇒ (300/x) – 300/(x + 10) = 5

⇒ [300(x + 10) – 300x]/x(x + 10) = 5

⇒ [300x + 3000 – 300x] = 5x(x + 10)

⇒ 3000 = 5x2 + 50x

⇒ 5x2 + 50x – 3000 = 0

⇒ x2 + 10x – 600 = 0

⇒ x2 + 30x – 20x – 600 = 0

⇒ x(x + 30) – 20(x + 30) = 0

⇒ (x – 20)(x + 30) = 0

⇒ x = 20, -30

⇒ x = 20km/h as negative speed is not possible.

∴ The speed for the outward journey is 20km/h

Shortcut Trick Concept:

[(Speed 1 × Speed 2) / Speed difference] × Time difference = Total distance

Calculation:

Let the speed of outward journey be ‘x’ km/h

Hence, the speed of return journey will be (x + 10) km/h

So, 

\(\frac{x \times (x+10)}{10} \times 5 = 300\)

⇒ \(x \times (x+10) = 600\)

⇒ \(x \times (x+10) = 20 \times 30\)

⇒ x = 20

∴ The speed for the outward journey is 20km/h

questions.question: Tom travelled 285 km in 6 hours. In his total travelling, he travelled the first part by bus at 40 km/hr and the remaining part by train at 55 km/hr. How much distance has he travelled by train?
questions.questionHtml: Tom travelled 285 km in 6 hours. In his total travelling, he travelled the first part by bus at 40 km/hr and the remaining part by train at 55 km/hr. How much distance has he travelled by train?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total distance = 285 km

Total time = 6 hours

Speed by bus = 40 km/hr

Speed by train = 55 km/hr

Let distance travelled by bus = x km

Formula used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Total time = Time by bus + Time by train

Calculations:

Time by bus = x ÷ 40

Time by train = (285 - x) ÷ 55

Total time = 6 hours

⇒ x ÷ 40 + (285 - x) ÷ 55 = 6

⇒ (55x + 40(285 - x)) ÷ (40 × 55) = 6

⇒ (55x + 11400 - 40x) ÷ 2200 = 6

⇒ (15x + 11400) ÷ 2200 = 6

⇒ 15x + 11400 = 13200

⇒ 15x = 13200 - 11400

⇒ 15x = 1800

⇒ x = 1800 ÷ 15

⇒ x = 120 km

Distance travelled by train = 285 - 120 = 165 km

∴ Distance travelled by train = 165 km

questions.question: A car starts running at an initial speed of 60 km/h, with its speed increasing every hour by 10 km/h. How many hours will it take to cover a distance of 1210 km?
questions.questionHtml: A car starts running at an initial speed of 60 km/h, with its speed increasing every hour by 10 km/h. How many hours will it take to cover a distance of 1210 km?
questions.solution:
Sn = (n/2) × {2a + (n - 1) × d} = 1210 = (n/2) × {2 × 60 + (n -1) × 10}

⇒ 2 × 1210  = n × {120 + (n - 1) × 10} ⇒ n2 + 11n - 242 = 0 ⇒ (n + 22) (n - 11) = 0

⇒ (n - 11) = 0 ⇒ n = 11

questions.question: A car moves at the speed of 108 km / hr after repairing and moves at the speed of 72 km / hr before repairing. It covers a distance of x km in 3 hours after repairing. How much time will it take to cover a distance of 5 x km before repairing?

Time before repairing = 1620/72 ⇒ 135/6 = 22 hours 30 minutes.

questions.question: Two trains start at the same time from two stations and proceed towards each other at speeds of 90 km/h and 70 km/h, respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 140 km more than the other. What is the distance (in km) between the two stations?
questions.questionHtml: Two trains start at the same time from two stations and proceed towards each other at speeds of 90 km/h and 70 km/h, respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 140 km more than the other. What is the distance (in km) between the two stations?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of trains are respectively 90 km/ hr and 70 km / hr

One train travelled 140 km more than other

Formula used:

Distance= Speed ×  Time

Calculations :

Let the time of traveling be ' t ' hour's

Distance travelled by train with speed 90 km/h = 90 × t = 90t 

Distance travelled by train with speed 70 km/h = 70 × t = 70t 

According to the question 

Difference in distance traveled by two train = 140 km

90 × t - 70 × t = 140

⇒ 90t - 70t = 140

⇒ 20t = 140

⇒ t = 7 hours

Distance between stations = 90 × 7 + 70 × 7

⇒ 160 × 7

⇒ 1120 km

∴ The correct choice is option 2.

Alternate MethodIf time is constant then 

Ratio of speed = ratio of distance

So, Ratio of speed = 90 : 70 = 9 : 7

Ratio of Distance = 9 : 7

⇒ (9 - 7) = 2 units = 140 km

⇒ 1 unit = 70 km

Then total distance = (70 × 9) + (70 × 7)

⇒ 630 + 490 = 1120 km

∴ The correct answer is 1120 km.

Shortcut Trick We know that 

Distance = Time × Speed

That means the distance will be the factor of speed.

Now the relative speed = 90 + 70 = 160 km/hr

Now we will check whether option will be divisible by 160.

Only the second option is the factor of the given speed.

Hence, the distance is 1120 km.

questions.question: A man travelled a distance of 1200 km in 16 hours. He travelled partly by car at a speed of 40 km/h, and partly by train at a speed of 80 km/h. What is the distance travelled by car?
questions.questionHtml: A man travelled a distance of 1200 km in 16 hours. He travelled partly by car at a speed of 40 km/h, and partly by train at a speed of 80 km/h. What is the distance travelled by car?
questions.solution:
Given :

A man travelled a distance of 1200 km in 16 hours. He travelled partly by car at a speed of 40 km/h, and partly by train at a speed of 80 km/h.

Concept used :

Time = Distance/speed 

Calculations :

Let the distance travelled with 80 km/h speed be 'x' km 

Let the distance travelled with 40 km/h speed be '1200 - x' km 

Time for x km = x/80 

Time for 1200 - x km = (1200 - x)/40 

Total time = (x/80) + (1200 - x)/40 

⇒ (x/80) + (1200 - x)/40 = 16 

⇒ x = 1120 km 

Distance travelled by car = 1200 - x 

⇒ 1200 - 1120 

⇒ 80 km. 

∴ Option 2 will be the right answer. 

Shortcut TrickCalculation:

Speed of man's overall journey = 1200/16 = 75 km/hr

Now,

Ratio of time = 1 : 7

So (1 + 7) = 8 units = 16 hrs

⇒ 1 unit = 2 hrs

So distance travelled by car = 40 × 2 = 80 km.

∴ The correct answer is 80 km.

questions.question: The speed of a car increases by 2 km/h after every one hour. If the distance travelled in the first one hour was 35 km, what was the total distance travelled in 12 hours?
questions.questionHtml: The speed of a car increases by 2 km/h after every one hour. If the distance travelled in the first one hour was 35 km, what was the total distance travelled in 12 hours?
questions.solution:
Given∶

Speed of car increases after every hour = 2 km/h

Distance travelled in 1st one hour = 35 km

Calculation∶

Distance travelled in 2nd hour = 35 + 2 = 37 km

Distance travelled in 3rd hour = 37 + 2 = 39 km

∴ Distance travelled by car in every hour will be in Arithmetic Progression.

35, 37, 39… up to 12 terms

First term = a = 35, common difference = d = 37 – 35 = 2, number of terms = n = 12

Formula∶ Sum of n terms of an Arithmetic Progression = n/2{2a + (n – 1)d}

∴ Total distance travelled in 12 hours = 12/2{2 × 35 + (12 – 1)2} = 6(70 + 22) = 6 × 92 = 552 km

questions.question: A man travels the first part of his journey at 80 km/h and the second part at 120 km/h, and covers a total distance of 3840 km to his destination in 40 hours. How long did the first part of his journey last?
questions.questionHtml: A man travels the first part of his journey at 80 km/h and the second part at 120 km/h, and covers a total distance of 3840 km to his destination in 40 hours. How long did the first part of his journey last?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total distance = 3840 km 

Total time taken = 40 hours

Two speed are 80 km/h and 120 km/h.

Formula used:

Speed = Distance/Time

Calculation:

Let the distance covered at 80 km/h be 'x' km.

⇒ Remaining distance covered at 120 km/h = (3840 – x) km

Time taken to covered x km = (x/80)

⇒ Time taken to covered (3840 – x) km = [(3840 – x)/60]

According to the question,

(x/80) +  [(3840 – x)/120] = 40

⇒ [3x + 7680 – 2x]/240 = 40

⇒ x + 7680 = 9600

⇒ x = 1920

So, first part of his journey last = 1920/80 = 24 hours

∴  First part of his journey last in 24 hours.

questions.question: A car travels a distance of 60 km at uniform speed, If the speed of car is increased by 8 km/hr, then it takes 2 hours less to cover the same distance. What is the original speed of the car?
questions.questionHtml: A car travels a distance of 60 km at uniform speed, If the speed of car is increased by 8 km/hr, then it takes 2 hours less to cover the same distance. What is the original speed of the car?
questions.solution:
Time taken to cover the same distance at the increased speed = 60 / (s + 8) hours

⇒ 60/s - 60/(s + 8) = 2 ⇒ 60(s+8) - 60s = 2s(s+8) ⇒ 2s2 + 16s - 480 = 0

Dividing both sides by 2, \(s^2 + 8s - 240 = 0\) ⇒ (s+20)(s-12) = 0 ⇒ s = 12.

questions.question: Ranjeet drives his car at an average speed of 50 km/hr and reaches his destination in 8 hours. Rahman covers the same distance in 5 hours. If Ranjeet increases his speed by 10 km/hr and Rahman increases his speed by 20 km/hr, then what will be the difference in time taken by them to reach their destination?
questions.questionHtml: Ranjeet drives his car at an average speed of 50 km/hr and reaches his destination in 8 hours. Rahman covers the same distance in 5 hours. If Ranjeet increases his speed by 10 km/hr and Rahman increases his speed by 20 km/hr, then what will be the difference in time taken by them to reach their destination?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of Ranjeet = 50 km/hr

Calculation:

Total distance covered by Ranjeet in 8 hrs = 50 × 8 = 400 km

Speed of Rahman = 400/5 = 80 km/hr

New speed of Ranjeet = 50 + 10 = 60 km/hr

New speed of Rahman = 80 + 20 = 100 km/hr

Time taken by Ranjeet to cover 400 km distance = 400/60 = 6 hr 40 min

Time taken by Rahman to cover 400 km distance = 400/100 = 4 hr

Required difference = 6 hr + 40 min – 4 hr = 2 hours 40 minutes

questions.question: With a uniform speed, a car covers a distance in 16 hours. Had the speed been increased by 20 km/h, the same distance would have been covered in 12 hours. The total distance covered by the car is:
questions.questionHtml: With a uniform speed, a car covers a distance in 16 hours. Had the speed been increased by 20 km/h, the same distance would have been covered in 12 hours. The total distance covered by the car is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional.

Ratio of Time = 16 : 12 = 4 : 3 ⇒ Ratio of Speed = 3 : 4

Difference in speed ratio (1 unit) = 20 km/h

Original speed = 3 units = 60 km/h

Total distance = 60 km/h × 16 h = 960 km

∴ The correct answer is 960 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken at original speed = 16 hours

Time taken at increased speed = 12 hours

Increase in speed = 20 km/h

Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

Let the original speed be S km/h.

Since the distance covered in both cases is the same:

⇒ Distance1 = Distance2

⇒ S × 16 = (S + 20) × 12

⇒ 16S = 12S + 240

⇒ 16S − 12S = 240

⇒ 4S = 240

⇒ S = 60 km/h

Now, calculate the total distance covered by the car:

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance = 60 × 16 = 960 km

∴ The correct answer is 960 km.

Additional Information

Proportionality in Speed, Time, and Distance

If Distance is constant, Speed ∝ 1 / Time. If Time is constant, Distance ∝ Speed. If Speed is constant, Distance ∝ Time.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. For equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = |S1 − S2|. In opposite directions, relative speed = S1 + S2.

questions.question: With an average speed of 45 km/h, a train reaches its destination on time. If it goes with an average speed of 30 km/h, it is late by 15 minutes. The total journey is:
questions.questionHtml: With an average speed of 45 km/h, a train reaches its destination on time. If it goes with an average speed of 30 km/h, it is late by 15 minutes. The total journey is:
questions.solution: Total distance = \(\frac{(S_1 × S_2)}{S_1-S_2}\) × (time difference) = \(\frac{(45 × 30)}{45-30} × \frac{15}{60}\) ⇒ 22.5 km

questions.question: A goes to a mall from his house on a cycle at 8 km/h and comes back to his house on a cycle at 6 km/h. If he takes 1 hour 10 minutes in all, what is the distance between his house and the mall?
questions.questionHtml: A goes to a mall from his house on a cycle at 8 km/h and comes back to his house on a cycle at 6 km/h. If he takes 1 hour 10 minutes in all, what is the distance between his house and the mall?
questions.solution:
As we know, 1 hr + 10 min = 70/60 hr

Let the distance between house and mall be x km

According to the question

x/8 + x/6 = 70/60 hr

7x/24 = 70/60

x = 70/60 × 24/7 = 4 km
